page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2.0 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64s_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. While single-core stress-ng performance is average, multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks for both read and write operations reach top-tier status in the top 10%, though the overall PassMark memory score remains average. The system excels in database operations and multi-core Geekbench tests, placing in the top 10%. It also shows strong performance in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and LLM inference tasks across various model sizes.

A primary hardware tradeoff of the E64s_v6 is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external Premium Storage volumes for data persistence. It also lacks integrated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU combined with strong multi-threaded performance makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of GPU accelerators. This profile is highly suited for large database operations, enterprise applications, memory-cached web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
